rationale: C20 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both are presidential letters to the Civil Aeronautics Board concerning a pending Pacific aviation case, revisit an earlier presidential position because of subsequently received information or changed circumstances, and conclude by requesting further Board action in that case. C18 has highly similar CAB-letter language and the identical addressee, but its operative structure is more simply a partial approval followed by a request for a revised order. C16 shares a request for agency review and reporting but lacks the distinctive aviation-case and reconsideration framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I advised the Board on February 1, 1955 that I desired to hold in abeyance my decision ... pending further study and later report
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I desire to amend my letter of February first with reference to the West Coast-Hawaii Case.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by revisiting a February 1 presidential disposition of a Pacific air-route proceeding.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have been advised, however, that new circumstances and new developments have arisen
shared_material.parent_excerpt: since my original action in this case I have received from you information to the effect that within two years all air line subsidies in the Pacific area will probably have been eliminated
shared_material.explanation: Each makes new information arising after the original action the reason for reconsidering the matter.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I, therefore, request the Board to consider the case in the light of any new and relevant circumstances or developments that it finds to exist, and advise me as soon as possible as to its findings and conclusions thereon.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accordingly, I request the Board present for my approval a revised order in this case
shared_material.explanation: Both culminate in the same transition and operative mechanism: a presidential request that the Board take renewed action in the pending case.
